title: Compatibility corridor for chunked-SSE and longpoll endpoint migration
creator: Priya Menon
description: PRD-style playbook that defines the compatibility corridor, migration requirements, and acceptance criteria for decommissioning legacy chunked-SSE and longpoll endpoints in favor of the unified streaming API. Covers engineering deliverables, SDK shims, migration timeline, telemetry gates, and customer communication cadence.
background: We operate two legacy transport flavors (chunked-SSE and HTTP longpoll) that predate the unified streaming/response model. These transports increase maintenance cost, fragment monitoring, and block uniform routing/optimization strategies (batching, KV cache reuse). Product goal: consolidate runtimes onto the unified streaming endpoint while minimizing customer disruption and preserving the ability to roll back quickly.
requirements: Server-side: stable 302/301 alias mapping layer to route legacy requests to the compatibility corridor during the opt-in phase
Server-side: configurable feature-flag per-customer to enable/disable redirect behavior and shadowing
SDK: publish a lightweight compatibility shim (node/python/go) that translates chunked-SSE and longpoll client patterns to the unified streaming API and surfaces equivalent reconnect/error semantics
Docs: migration guide, sample code snippets, FAQ, and an automated CLI migration tester for major client languages
Monitoring: new telemetry keys for legacy transport usage, conversion success rate, latency delta, error classification, and silent-fallback occurrences
Rollout tooling: gradual redirect percentages, per-customer gates, and emergency rollback toggle
Legal/enterprise: written notification templates and opt-out support for Dedicated/Private deployments
Testing: end-to-end compatibility test harness and a suite of acceptance tests covering edge cases (intermittent disconnects, partial payloads, rewind semantics)
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility shim published with stable semver and sample integrations for Node, Python, and Go
Server-side aliasing and redirect mechanism validated in staging with <0.5% error delta compared to baseline for representative workloads
Shadowing run completed for at least 3 production customers across different traffic shapes for 14 days with no >2x error increase and documented issues triaged
Automated migration tester available and passing in nightly CI for the three supported languages
Customer-facing migration docs reviewed by DX and Legal and published in the docs site
Telemetry dashboards show conversion rate, latency delta, and per-customer impact; SLO gates configured (see telemetry_and_gates)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Discovery, 2 weeks): inventory customers using chunked-SSE/longpoll, collect client SDK versions, and map Dedicated/Private installs
Phase 1 (Shadow, 3 weeks): enable server-side shadow routing for opt-in customers and begin telemetry collection; no customer-visible redirect
Phase 2 (Opt-in redirect, 4 weeks): offer per-customer opt-in redirect with compatibility shim available; monitor telemetry and provide support
Phase 3 (Graduated enforcement, 8 weeks): increase redirect percentages for non-critical customers, continue enterprise coordination for Dedicated/Private
Phase 4 (Warning + final cutoff announcements, 12 weeks): send final warning emails and deprecate endpoints with a 90-day grace period before hard removal
Phase 5 (Decommission): remove legacy transport code-paths and close feature flags; ensure archived telemetry and incident runbook available
migration_guidance: Encourage customers to adopt the compatibility shim first and run it in 'shadow' mode alongside existing clients
Provide sample conversion scripts for server-side reconnect/replay semantics when transitioning from longpoll to streaming
For WebSocket-based third-party proxies, offer an adapter recipe in the SDK that maps event envelopes to the unified response format
Enterprise Dedicated/Private: coordinate a dedicated migration window and provide on-call engineering support; allow longer grace periods per contract
Offer a migration CLI that validates a customer’s current usage against known incompatible patterns and returns actionable fixes
telemetry_and_gates: Gate A: conversion success rate must be >= 98% for 72-hour rolling window for a customer to progress from shadow to opt-in
Gate B: 95th percentile token latency regression < 10% relative to baseline or explicit acceptance from customer
Gate C: error-classification shows no new high-severity failure modes (disconnect storms, silent truncation) for 7 days
Gate D: business metrics — no customer-reported data-loss incidents; support queue trend must be stable or decreasing
rollback_criteria: Sustained >3% increase in customer error-rate tied to compatibility corridor for 24+ hours
A single-severity incident that impacts >5% of requests or causes data corruption
Unresolvable regressions in kms/authorization flow discovered during opt-in
Enterprises explicitly request rollback due to contractual obligations or regulatory concerns
open_questions: How should we treat third-party SDKs that embed legacy behavior with no upgrade path?
What is the minimum contractual notice period required for Dedicated customers in EMEA?
Do Dedicated/Private installs require an on-prem compatibility package that differs from hosted SDK shims?
Should we introduce a ‘compatibility compatibility’ flag in the Console for non-engineering admins?

2026-03-05: Prototype compatibility shim (node) initial release on internal registry; basic tests passed in staging.
